strings: Hilbert’s basis theorem says that if a commutative ring is Noetherian then its polynomial ring is Noetherian. In particular, every ideal of a polynomial ring over a field has finitely many generators.
Over an algebraically closed field, polynomials with no common zero generate the unit ideal. An identity Σgᵢfᵢ=1 certifies this: evaluating at a hypothetical common zero would give 0=1.
From Boolean formulas to proof complexity

Add xᵢ²−xᵢ=0 to restrict variables to Boolean values. The clause x∨y∨¬z becomes (1−x)(1−y)z=0. An unsatisfiable formula then admits an algebraic refutation, but its required degree and representation size may be large.
Randomization gives a game a value

For a finite payoff matrix A, a player chooses a probability vector over rows and the opponent one over columns. The minimax theorem equates the strongest guaranteed payoff with the smallest upper bound the opponent can enforce.

The stored-program architecture keeps encoded instructions in memory. A machine can therefore change tasks by loading a different program. The EDVAC report helped spread this design; sole-inventor accounts overlook Eckert, Mauchly and the wider engineering collaboration.
Von Neumann’s Hilbert-space approach organized quantum states and observables. His work with Murray on operator algebras generated a major field with lasting connections to mathematical physics.

The completeness theorem says that first-order deduction captures every consequence true in all models of a theory. Incompleteness concerns a different issue: no consistent, effectively axiomatized theory sufficiently strong for arithmetic decides every arithmetic sentence. A truth in the intended natural numbers need not hold in every model of the axioms.

Gödel assigns natural-number codes to formulas and proofs. Arithmetic can then express a relation saying that one number encodes a proof of the formula encoded by another. A diagonal construction produces a sentence asserting its own unprovability. Rosser’s refinement obtains undecidability from consistency alone.
What the limit does not say

The result does not say that a particular true sentence can never be proved in a stronger theory. It says that no single effective consistent arithmetic theory supplies all answers. Gödel also constructed the universe L, establishing relative consistency results for choice and the continuum hypothesis.

A finite transition rule controls a tape, a read/write head and a state. Encoding such a rule lets a single universal machine simulate every other machine. Programs themselves become manipulable data.

Assume a total procedure decides whether any program halts on any input. Construct D so that D(M) loops if that procedure predicts M(M) halts, and halts otherwise. Applying D to itself forces either answer to be wrong.

SAT is decidable by exhaustive search, even when that is expensive. Halting has no total deciding algorithm at all. Turing’s later contributions to cryptanalysis and machine intelligence do not erase this fundamental distinction.
In G(n,1/2), a fixed k-set is a clique or independent set with probability 2^{1−C(k,2)}. If C(n,k) times this probability is below one, some graph has neither.

Erdős proved that graphs can simultaneously have arbitrarily large girth and chromatic number. A random construction creates few short cycles and a small independence number; deleting selected vertices removes the cycles while retaining a large chromatic lower bound.
What the theorem does not control

This unrestricted construction does not settle high-girth coloring questions at one fixed small maximum degree. Keeping degree bounded is an extra structural demand. With Rényi, Erdős also developed the systematic study of phase transitions in random graphs.
An outcome of probability p has surprisal −log₂p. Averaging this over the source distribution gives entropy. A highly biased bit has entropy below one because its outcome is usually predictable.

Source coding concerns how far information can be compressed. Channel coding concerns how fast it can be transmitted reliably through noise. For a discrete memoryless channel, rates strictly below capacity allow codes with error tending to zero as block length grows.
Zero-error communication is a different requirement from vanishing error. Confusability can be represented by a graph, leading to Shannon capacity and Lovász’s solution for the five-cycle.

A profile is a Nash equilibrium when no player can improve while all other strategies remain fixed. It need not maximize total welfare. A jointly beneficial deviation may exist even when no profitable unilateral deviation exists.

Mixed strategies form a product of simplices. One can construct a continuous map that moves probability toward actions with positive improvement. At a fixed point, no such improvement remains. Brouwer’s theorem supplies existence.

For rational two-player games, an equilibrium has a polynomial-bit rational representation and finding one is PPAD-complete. Exact equilibria of games with at least three players may be irrational and require a more careful formulation, involving FIXP rather than a blanket TFNP claim.
The equations x=0 and x²=0 have the same ordinary zero set. Their coordinate rings differ: k[x]/(x²) retains a nonzero nilpotent element. A scheme remembers information that the bare set loses.
Spec(A) is built from prime ideals together with a structure sheaf. Working over Spec(Z) allows one geometric family to be studied over Q and over finite fields through changes of base.

For X=Spec(A), its R-points are ring homomorphisms A→R, with the appropriate base compatibility. This functor-of-points viewpoint shifts attention from isolated coordinates to how a space interacts with all test objects.

Schemes and étale cohomology transformed arithmetic geometry. Geometric complexity theory uses algebraic geometry and invariant theory, but a direct historical claim that Grothendieck invented GCT would be wrong.

Cook–Levin encodes arbitrary NP computations as satisfiability. Karp then used reductions among concrete problems to establish widespread NP-completeness. The direction matters: to show B is hard, reduce a known hard A to B.
A k-clique in G is an independent set of size k in its complement. The complement of an independent set is a vertex cover. Thus the instance (G,k) becomes (Ḡ,n−k) for Vertex Cover.
The implication, not an unconditional lower bound

NP-completeness says a polynomial-time exact algorithm would imply P=NP. It is not a proof of exponential running time. The framework motivates approximation, parameterization and special-case algorithms. Karp’s later randomized work includes string fingerprints with Rabin.

The symmetric Local Lemma gives positive probability of avoiding all bad events if each has probability at most p and a dependency graph has degree at most d with ep(d+1)≤1. Each event must be independent of the sigma-algebra generated by its nonneighbors, not merely pairwise independent of them.

One formulation of theta maximizes ⟨J,X⟩ subject to tr(X)=1, X⪰0 and Xᵢⱼ=0 on edges. An independent set gives a feasible matrix, so α(G)≤ϑ(G). Multiplicativity gives an upper bound for Shannon capacity.

Lovász’s topological proof of Kneser’s conjecture and his work on graphons both replace a finite combinatorial problem with a richer object. Dense graphons and bounded-degree graphings are different limit frameworks.

A #P function counts polynomial-size witnesses accepted by a polynomial-time relation. Asking whether a bipartite graph has a perfect matching is polynomial-time; counting all perfect matchings is #P-complete. This does not unconditionally separate their running times.

VP consists of polynomial-degree families with polynomial-size arithmetic circuits. VNP permits an exponential Boolean summation of efficiently computed polynomials. The permanent is VNP-complete under projections over fields of characteristic different from two. In characteristic two it equals the determinant.
PAC learning separates accuracy ε, failure probability δ, sample complexity and running time. A class can be statistically learnable yet computationally hard to learn under cryptographic assumptions.

On Boolean inputs, negation is 1−x, conjunction is xy, and disjunction is x+y−xy. Universal quantification multiplies the two evaluations; existential quantification takes their Boolean OR. Summation alone is not existential quantification.

Repeated quantifiers can double individual degrees. Replace p by its multilinearization in x: this preserves its values at x=0 and x=1 while reducing its degree in x to one. The protocol verifies these reductions rather than writing out an exponential expression.

The prover sends a low-degree univariate polynomial, then the verifier samples a field point. Distinct degree-d polynomials agree at at most d points. Following a sequence of such challenges reduces a huge claim to a final directly checkable evaluation.

An exponentially large field still has polynomial-length element descriptions. The key issue is not cardinality alone: an exponentially high-degree polynomial is too long to transmit in the coefficient representation used by the protocol.
A proof is now a protocol

Goldwasser, Micali and Rackoff introduced a model in which a randomized efficient verifier interacts with a powerful prover. Completeness guarantees honest success; soundness limits even computationally unbounded cheating provers.

For every allowed cheating verifier, a simulator without the secret witness must reproduce its view in the appropriate exact, statistical or computational sense. Merely withholding the witness is not enough.

Send a random relabeling H of one graph, then answer a challenge asking for an isomorphism from G₀ or G₁ to H. An honest-verifier transcript can be simulated by choosing the challenge first. General zero knowledge also needs a simulator handling a verifier whose challenge depends on H; the standard analysis uses rewinding.
Search a group rather than all permutations

Graph isomorphism asks for an adjacency-preserving bijection. Permutation groups can be represented by a small list of generators, while their orbits, stabilizers and cosets organize the candidate maps.

Color refinement distinguishes vertices by recursively aggregating neighborhood information. Babai’s algorithm combines more powerful combinatorial analysis with local certificates and permutation-group structure. The structural dichotomy is much more precise than “symmetric graphs are hard.”

Babai introduced Arthur–Merlin games and, with Fortnow and Lund, proved MIP=NEXP. His graph-isomorphism work and his interactive-proof work connect through complexity but should not be confused as the same algorithm.
An unrestricted Boolean circuit uses AND, OR and NOT. Monotone circuits omit NOT. Razborov proved strong lower bounds in this restricted setting, including for clique, using an approximation method.
Razborov–Smolensky methods approximate small constant-depth circuits with MOD-p gates by low-degree polynomials over Fₚ. Functions with incompatible modular behavior resist such approximations.

Razborov and Rudich identified a barrier to properties that are large, efficiently recognizable from a truth table, and useful against small circuits. Under sufficiently strong pseudorandom-function assumptions, such properties would distinguish pseudorandom functions from random ones. Truth-table efficiency is exponential in the number of input variables.
A seed generator has support much smaller than the full random-bit space. It can still fool a bounded class of computations if their acceptance probabilities change by at most ε.

An S-space computation has only exponentially many possible configurations. In the standard bounded-space model, Nisan’s generator exploits this restriction to reduce randomness dramatically; a common summary is seed length O(S log R), with the model and error conditions understood.

With Wigderson, Nisan used carefully overlapping subsets of a seed to evaluate a hard function many times. A distinguisher can be converted into a predictor. Hardness amplification and parameter control are needed to turn worst-case hardness into a full derandomization theorem.
A circuit lower bound becomes an algorithm

Nisan–Wigderson generators evaluate a hard function on overlapping portions of a seed. Small intersections let one convert a distinguisher into a small predictor. Impagliazzo–Wigderson hardness amplification supplies the bridge from suitable worst-case hardness.

A BPP algorithm using polynomially many random bits can be simulated by trying every seed when a suitable efficiently evaluable generator has O(log n) seed length. The number of seeds is then polynomial.

A separate theorem of Kabanets and Impagliazzo says that sufficiently strong derandomization of arithmetic polynomial identity testing implies a major Boolean or arithmetic circuit lower bound. It should not be attributed to Wigderson, nor simplified to an unconditional arithmetic lower bound alone.

P/poly permits a separate polynomial-size circuit for each input length. There need not be an efficient algorithm that constructs those circuits. Uniform algorithms are therefore a stricter resource model.

Assume SAT has small circuits. A SAT decision circuit can choose the bits of a satisfying assignment by self-reduction. For a statement ∀y∃z R(x,y,z), existentially guess such a witness-producing circuit, then universally verify R(x,y,C(y)).

A false statement has some y with no witness z. No guessed circuit can output a valid witness on that y. With polynomial circuit bounds, this puts Π₂ᴾ inside Σ₂ᴾ and collapses PH. Lipton’s separate work with DeMillo helped develop randomized algebraic identity checking.

For simple random walk on Zᵈ, recurrence is equivalent to divergence of the sum of return probabilities. On even times those probabilities behave like n^{−d/2}, giving recurrence exactly in dimensions one and two.

Burnside’s averaging counts orbits. Pólya’s cycle index refines it to track inventories of colors. For rotations of a square, the cycle index is (a₁⁴+a₂²+2a₄)/4; substituting every aᵢ=2 gives six binary colorings.

How to Solve It emphasizes changing representations, working backward and solving simpler cases. These are heuristics for finding a proof, not inference rules that establish correctness by themselves.

Multiple provers may coordinate before the protocol but cannot communicate during it. The verifier can send related questions whose connection is hidden from either prover. Their answers must agree with a common global account.

An NEXP computation can have an exponentially large witness. The BFL theorem encodes such a witness so that a polynomial-time verifier can perform algebraic and consistency checks without reading the whole object.

A nonadaptive local verifier can be converted into a constraint system with one constraint for each random string. Its completeness–soundness gap becomes an optimization gap. Deriving the full PCP theorem requires additional results; it is not immediate from the equality alone.
The communication rule does not change
Entangled provers remain unable to communicate during the protocol. They may share a state and answer by local measurements, producing correlations not available to classical shared randomness.

Ji, Natarajan, Vidick, Wright and Yuen proved that finite-dimensional entangled multiprover verification with a completeness–soundness gap captures recursively enumerable languages. The allowed finite dimension is not bounded in advance by a computable function of the input.
Do not confuse verification with decision
The verifier alone does not decide membership. Finding or bounding the necessary prover strategy is the source of noncomputability. The result also has consequences for operator-algebra problems.

An OR of three distinct noncontradictory literals is false on exactly one of eight assignments. A uniformly random assignment therefore satisfies 7m/8 clauses in expectation, and conditional expectations can remove the randomness.
A constant gap is the key

Ordinary NP-hardness may separate full satisfaction from failure on one clause out of millions. Approximation hardness requires a robust gap. Håstad constructed PCPs giving essentially optimal gaps for MAX-E3SAT and MAX-E3LIN.
Decode a coordinate from a function

Long-code tests encode a label i as the dictator f(x)=xᵢ. Fourier analysis shows how unusually high acceptance reveals coordinates usable as labels. The test and predicate determine the quantitative hardness.
The constraint is uniquely satisfiable in one direction

Every edge carries a permutation π, requiring xᵥ=π(xᵤ). Once one endpoint label is chosen, the other is forced. Exact full satisfiability can be tested by propagation; the conjecture concerns robust approximation gaps.

The Unique Games Conjecture posits NP-hardness of distinguishing optimum at least 1−ε from optimum at most δ, for every fixed positive ε and δ with a sufficiently large fixed alphabet. Consequences below are conditional on this conjecture, not unconditional hardness theorems.

Khot, Kindler, Mossel and O’Donnell related MAX-CUT hardness to noise stability. Conditional on UGC, beating the Goemans–Williamson ratio by a fixed amount would be NP-hard. Raghavendra extended the relationship to a general fixed-CSP framework.
The characters χS(x)=∏ᵢ∈Sxᵢ form an orthonormal basis under the uniform measure on {−1,1}ⁿ. Every real-valued function on the cube has a unique expansion.
If each coordinate pair has correlation ρ, noise stability is ΣSρ^{|S|}f̂(S)². High-degree components are damped when |ρ|<1. For Boolean-valued f, coordinate influence is ΣS∋ᵢf̂(S)².

For fixed positive noise correlation, balanced Boolean functions with sufficiently small coordinate influences have stability at most the asymptotic majority value plus a small error. The Mossel–O’Donnell–Oleszkiewicz invariance principle transfers the problem toward Gaussian space.
A cut assigns each vertex a sign xᵢ. Its objective is Σwᵢⱼ(1−xᵢxⱼ)/2 for nonnegative edge weights. Replacing signs by unit vectors relaxes the discrete problem to an SDP.
Choose a rotationally symmetric Gaussian vector g and use the sign of ⟨g,vᵢ⟩. Two vectors at angle θ are separated with probability θ/π. Compare this with their SDP contribution (1−cosθ)/2.

The expected cut value is at least αGW times the SDP value and hence at least αGW times the true optimum, up to numerical precision. UGC-based hardness gives a matching threshold, but that optimality statement is conditional.

Fix a finite domain and a finite set of bounded-arity predicates. The task is to maximize the fraction or weight of satisfied constraints. This framework includes many, but not all, optimization problems.

The basic SDP combines vector correlations with local distributions on constraint scopes. Pairwise inner products alone do not describe arbitrary higher-arity constraints. A genuine assignment gives a feasible solution, while an SDP solution may not correspond to any global assignment.

Raghavendra connects the achievable rounding guarantees to matching Unique-Games-based hardness, with arbitrarily small slack. The theorem turns a problem-by-problem approximation search into a unified framework, though finding a simple closed-form threshold may still be difficult.

A distribution on Boolean assignments determines moments of every monomial. A relaxation retains moments only through degree 2d, expressed as a linear functional Ẽ. It must normalize 1 and annihilate the equality constraints at allowed degrees.
For monomials xᵅ of degree at most d, form Mᵅᵝ=Ẽ[xᵅ⁺ᵝ]. Requiring Ẽ[p²]≥0 for every degree-d polynomial p is equivalent to M being positive semidefinite.

As the level rises, feasible truncated moment sets become more restricted, and maximization upper bounds decrease. For Boolean problems, sufficiently high levels are exact. Fixed levels have SDP size n^{O(d)}, with numerical precision conditions still relevant.

The dual seeks bounded-degree sum-of-squares certificates modulo the constraints. General polynomial optimization needs appropriate compactness or positivity assumptions for convergence claims. A pseudoexpectation obstructs a low-degree certificate without necessarily describing a real probability measure.

The vertex update records a vertex’s old color and the multiset of its neighbors’ colors. Assign equal new colors exactly when these records agree. Run comparison with a common encoding, not unrelated color names in each graph.

Starting from one color, every vertex of a d-regular graph sees the same multiset forever. Two nonisomorphic d-regular graphs of equal order are therefore indistinguishable by this basic procedure. Rigidity and automorphism count are separate issues.

Higher-dimensional versions refine tuples. Precise correspondences with counting logic depend on conventions and indexing. Cai–Fürer–Immerman constructions give nonisomorphic graph families requiring linearly many variables to distinguish, exposing a global parity obstruction.

Directed reachability is NL-complete. Immerman and Szelepcsényi independently proved that its complement is in NL. The method tracks the number of vertices reachable within k steps rather than storing all of them.
Why a count makes the certificate trustworthy

Given the correct number of reachable vertices, a nondeterministic computation can enumerate witnessed reachable vertices and reject if the count is wrong. This supports an inductive update of the next reachable-set size using logarithmic workspace.

On finite structures equipped with a linear order, first-order logic with transitive closure captures NL, and least fixed-point logic captures P. The order hypothesis in the Immerman–Vardi theorem is essential to its stated form.

Every first-order sentence over a finite relational vocabulary is equivalent to a Boolean combination of basic local sentences. Such a sentence asks for finitely many sufficiently separated vertices, all satisfying a specified local formula.

For bounded-degree graph sequences, Benjamini–Schramm convergence records the probabilities of rooted neighborhoods. A rare feature can occur at one vertex and disappear from those probabilities, while an existential FO sentence still detects it.
Why algorithms need more than a radius

A fixed-radius ball can still be huge when degrees are unbounded. Algorithmic applications therefore combine locality with structural sparsity or other restrictions. Locality does not make arbitrary-graph model checking automatically easy.

Subdividing every edge of a clique once gives a graph of bounded average degree, but depth-one contractions recover the original clique. A useful sparsity notion must control what is revealed by local contraction.

Bounded expansion bounds the density of every fixed-depth shallow minor by a function of that depth. Nowhere density instead excludes sufficiently large clique shallow minors at each fixed depth. It is a weaker structural restriction.

Nešetřil and Ossona de Mendez developed the structural framework underlying important model-checking results. Dvořák–Král’–Thomas obtained linear-time FO model checking for bounded expansion, and Grohe–Kreutzer–Siebertz almost-linear algorithms for effectively nowhere-dense classes. Nešetřil’s work with Hell also made graph homomorphisms central to coloring and CSPs.

entries.text: Hilbert’s basis theorem says that if a commutative ring is Noetherian then its polynomial ring is Noetherian. In particular, every ideal of a polynomial ring over a field has finitely many generators.
Over an algebraically closed field, polynomials with no common zero generate the unit ideal. An identity Σgᵢfᵢ=1 certifies this: evaluating at a hypothetical common zero would give 0=1.
From Boolean formulas to proof complexity

Add xᵢ²−xᵢ=0 to restrict variables to Boolean values. The clause x∨y∨¬z becomes (1−x)(1−y)z=0. An unsatisfiable formula then admits an algebraic refutation, but its required degree and representation size may be large.
Randomization gives a game a value

For a finite payoff matrix A, a player chooses a probability vector over rows and the opponent one over columns. The minimax theorem equates the strongest guaranteed payoff with the smallest upper bound the opponent can enforce.

The stored-program architecture keeps encoded instructions in memory. A machine can therefore change tasks by loading a different program. The EDVAC report helped spread this design; sole-inventor accounts overlook Eckert, Mauchly and the wider engineering collaboration.
Von Neumann’s Hilbert-space approach organized quantum states and observables. His work with Murray on operator algebras generated a major field with lasting connections to mathematical physics.

The completeness theorem says that first-order deduction captures every consequence true in all models of a theory. Incompleteness concerns a different issue: no consistent, effectively axiomatized theory sufficiently strong for arithmetic decides every arithmetic sentence. A truth in the intended natural numbers need not hold in every model of the axioms.

Gödel assigns natural-number codes to formulas and proofs. Arithmetic can then express a relation saying that one number encodes a proof of the formula encoded by another. A diagonal construction produces a sentence asserting its own unprovability. Rosser’s refinement obtains undecidability from consistency alone.
What the limit does not say

The result does not say that a particular true sentence can never be proved in a stronger theory. It says that no single effective consistent arithmetic theory supplies all answers. Gödel also constructed the universe L, establishing relative consistency results for choice and the continuum hypothesis.

A finite transition rule controls a tape, a read/write head and a state. Encoding such a rule lets a single universal machine simulate every other machine. Programs themselves become manipulable data.

Assume a total procedure decides whether any program halts on any input. Construct D so that D(M) loops if that procedure predicts M(M) halts, and halts otherwise. Applying D to itself forces either answer to be wrong.

SAT is decidable by exhaustive search, even when that is expensive. Halting has no total deciding algorithm at all. Turing’s later contributions to cryptanalysis and machine intelligence do not erase this fundamental distinction.
In G(n,1/2), a fixed k-set is a clique or independent set with probability 2^{1−C(k,2)}. If C(n,k) times this probability is below one, some graph has neither.

Erdős proved that graphs can simultaneously have arbitrarily large girth and chromatic number. A random construction creates few short cycles and a small independence number; deleting selected vertices removes the cycles while retaining a large chromatic lower bound.
What the theorem does not control

This unrestricted construction does not settle high-girth coloring questions at one fixed small maximum degree. Keeping degree bounded is an extra structural demand. With Rényi, Erdős also developed the systematic study of phase transitions in random graphs.
An outcome of probability p has surprisal −log₂p. Averaging this over the source distribution gives entropy. A highly biased bit has entropy below one because its outcome is usually predictable.

Source coding concerns how far information can be compressed. Channel coding concerns how fast it can be transmitted reliably through noise. For a discrete memoryless channel, rates strictly below capacity allow codes with error tending to zero as block length grows.
Zero-error communication is a different requirement from vanishing error. Confusability can be represented by a graph, leading to Shannon capacity and Lovász’s solution for the five-cycle.

A profile is a Nash equilibrium when no player can improve while all other strategies remain fixed. It need not maximize total welfare. A jointly beneficial deviation may exist even when no profitable unilateral deviation exists.

Mixed strategies form a product of simplices. One can construct a continuous map that moves probability toward actions with positive improvement. At a fixed point, no such improvement remains. Brouwer’s theorem supplies existence.

For rational two-player games, an equilibrium has a polynomial-bit rational representation and finding one is PPAD-complete. Exact equilibria of games with at least three players may be irrational and require a more careful formulation, involving FIXP rather than a blanket TFNP claim.
The equations x=0 and x²=0 have the same ordinary zero set. Their coordinate rings differ: k[x]/(x²) retains a nonzero nilpotent element. A scheme remembers information that the bare set loses.
Spec(A) is built from prime ideals together with a structure sheaf. Working over Spec(Z) allows one geometric family to be studied over Q and over finite fields through changes of base.

For X=Spec(A), its R-points are ring homomorphisms A→R, with the appropriate base compatibility. This functor-of-points viewpoint shifts attention from isolated coordinates to how a space interacts with all test objects.

Schemes and étale cohomology transformed arithmetic geometry. Geometric complexity theory uses algebraic geometry and invariant theory, but a direct historical claim that Grothendieck invented GCT would be wrong.

Cook–Levin encodes arbitrary NP computations as satisfiability. Karp then used reductions among concrete problems to establish widespread NP-completeness. The direction matters: to show B is hard, reduce a known hard A to B.
A k-clique in G is an independent set of size k in its complement. The complement of an independent set is a vertex cover. Thus the instance (G,k) becomes (Ḡ,n−k) for Vertex Cover.
The implication, not an unconditional lower bound

NP-completeness says a polynomial-time exact algorithm would imply P=NP. It is not a proof of exponential running time. The framework motivates approximation, parameterization and special-case algorithms. Karp’s later randomized work includes string fingerprints with Rabin.

The symmetric Local Lemma gives positive probability of avoiding all bad events if each has probability at most p and a dependency graph has degree at most d with ep(d+1)≤1. Each event must be independent of the sigma-algebra generated by its nonneighbors, not merely pairwise independent of them.

One formulation of theta maximizes ⟨J,X⟩ subject to tr(X)=1, X⪰0 and Xᵢⱼ=0 on edges. An independent set gives a feasible matrix, so α(G)≤ϑ(G). Multiplicativity gives an upper bound for Shannon capacity.

Lovász’s topological proof of Kneser’s conjecture and his work on graphons both replace a finite combinatorial problem with a richer object. Dense graphons and bounded-degree graphings are different limit frameworks.

A #P function counts polynomial-size witnesses accepted by a polynomial-time relation. Asking whether a bipartite graph has a perfect matching is polynomial-time; counting all perfect matchings is #P-complete. This does not unconditionally separate their running times.

VP consists of polynomial-degree families with polynomial-size arithmetic circuits. VNP permits an exponential Boolean summation of efficiently computed polynomials. The permanent is VNP-complete under projections over fields of characteristic different from two. In characteristic two it equals the determinant.
PAC learning separates accuracy ε, failure probability δ, sample complexity and running time. A class can be statistically learnable yet computationally hard to learn under cryptographic assumptions.

On Boolean inputs, negation is 1−x, conjunction is xy, and disjunction is x+y−xy. Universal quantification multiplies the two evaluations; existential quantification takes their Boolean OR. Summation alone is not existential quantification.

Repeated quantifiers can double individual degrees. Replace p by its multilinearization in x: this preserves its values at x=0 and x=1 while reducing its degree in x to one. The protocol verifies these reductions rather than writing out an exponential expression.

The prover sends a low-degree univariate polynomial, then the verifier samples a field point. Distinct degree-d polynomials agree at at most d points. Following a sequence of such challenges reduces a huge claim to a final directly checkable evaluation.

An exponentially large field still has polynomial-length element descriptions. The key issue is not cardinality alone: an exponentially high-degree polynomial is too long to transmit in the coefficient representation used by the protocol.
A proof is now a protocol

Goldwasser, Micali and Rackoff introduced a model in which a randomized efficient verifier interacts with a powerful prover. Completeness guarantees honest success; soundness limits even computationally unbounded cheating provers.

For every allowed cheating verifier, a simulator without the secret witness must reproduce its view in the appropriate exact, statistical or computational sense. Merely withholding the witness is not enough.

Send a random relabeling H of one graph, then answer a challenge asking for an isomorphism from G₀ or G₁ to H. An honest-verifier transcript can be simulated by choosing the challenge first. General zero knowledge also needs a simulator handling a verifier whose challenge depends on H; the standard analysis uses rewinding.
Search a group rather than all permutations

Graph isomorphism asks for an adjacency-preserving bijection. Permutation groups can be represented by a small list of generators, while their orbits, stabilizers and cosets organize the candidate maps.

Color refinement distinguishes vertices by recursively aggregating neighborhood information. Babai’s algorithm combines more powerful combinatorial analysis with local certificates and permutation-group structure. The structural dichotomy is much more precise than “symmetric graphs are hard.”

Babai introduced Arthur–Merlin games and, with Fortnow and Lund, proved MIP=NEXP. His graph-isomorphism work and his interactive-proof work connect through complexity but should not be confused as the same algorithm.
An unrestricted Boolean circuit uses AND, OR and NOT. Monotone circuits omit NOT. Razborov proved strong lower bounds in this restricted setting, including for clique, using an approximation method.
Razborov–Smolensky methods approximate small constant-depth circuits with MOD-p gates by low-degree polynomials over Fₚ. Functions with incompatible modular behavior resist such approximations.

Razborov and Rudich identified a barrier to properties that are large, efficiently recognizable from a truth table, and useful against small circuits. Under sufficiently strong pseudorandom-function assumptions, such properties would distinguish pseudorandom functions from random ones. Truth-table efficiency is exponential in the number of input variables.
A seed generator has support much smaller than the full random-bit space. It can still fool a bounded class of computations if their acceptance probabilities change by at most ε.

An S-space computation has only exponentially many possible configurations. In the standard bounded-space model, Nisan’s generator exploits this restriction to reduce randomness dramatically; a common summary is seed length O(S log R), with the model and error conditions understood.

With Wigderson, Nisan used carefully overlapping subsets of a seed to evaluate a hard function many times. A distinguisher can be converted into a predictor. Hardness amplification and parameter control are needed to turn worst-case hardness into a full derandomization theorem.
A circuit lower bound becomes an algorithm

Nisan–Wigderson generators evaluate a hard function on overlapping portions of a seed. Small intersections let one convert a distinguisher into a small predictor. Impagliazzo–Wigderson hardness amplification supplies the bridge from suitable worst-case hardness.

A BPP algorithm using polynomially many random bits can be simulated by trying every seed when a suitable efficiently evaluable generator has O(log n) seed length. The number of seeds is then polynomial.

A separate theorem of Kabanets and Impagliazzo says that sufficiently strong derandomization of arithmetic polynomial identity testing implies a major Boolean or arithmetic circuit lower bound. It should not be attributed to Wigderson, nor simplified to an unconditional arithmetic lower bound alone.

P/poly permits a separate polynomial-size circuit for each input length. There need not be an efficient algorithm that constructs those circuits. Uniform algorithms are therefore a stricter resource model.

Assume SAT has small circuits. A SAT decision circuit can choose the bits of a satisfying assignment by self-reduction. For a statement ∀y∃z R(x,y,z), existentially guess such a witness-producing circuit, then universally verify R(x,y,C(y)).

A false statement has some y with no witness z. No guessed circuit can output a valid witness on that y. With polynomial circuit bounds, this puts Π₂ᴾ inside Σ₂ᴾ and collapses PH. Lipton’s separate work with DeMillo helped develop randomized algebraic identity checking.

For simple random walk on Zᵈ, recurrence is equivalent to divergence of the sum of return probabilities. On even times those probabilities behave like n^{−d/2}, giving recurrence exactly in dimensions one and two.

Burnside’s averaging counts orbits. Pólya’s cycle index refines it to track inventories of colors. For rotations of a square, the cycle index is (a₁⁴+a₂²+2a₄)/4; substituting every aᵢ=2 gives six binary colorings.

How to Solve It emphasizes changing representations, working backward and solving simpler cases. These are heuristics for finding a proof, not inference rules that establish correctness by themselves.

Multiple provers may coordinate before the protocol but cannot communicate during it. The verifier can send related questions whose connection is hidden from either prover. Their answers must agree with a common global account.

An NEXP computation can have an exponentially large witness. The BFL theorem encodes such a witness so that a polynomial-time verifier can perform algebraic and consistency checks without reading the whole object.

A nonadaptive local verifier can be converted into a constraint system with one constraint for each random string. Its completeness–soundness gap becomes an optimization gap. Deriving the full PCP theorem requires additional results; it is not immediate from the equality alone.
The communication rule does not change
Entangled provers remain unable to communicate during the protocol. They may share a state and answer by local measurements, producing correlations not available to classical shared randomness.

Ji, Natarajan, Vidick, Wright and Yuen proved that finite-dimensional entangled multiprover verification with a completeness–soundness gap captures recursively enumerable languages. The allowed finite dimension is not bounded in advance by a computable function of the input.
Do not confuse verification with decision
The verifier alone does not decide membership. Finding or bounding the necessary prover strategy is the source of noncomputability. The result also has consequences for operator-algebra problems.

An OR of three distinct noncontradictory literals is false on exactly one of eight assignments. A uniformly random assignment therefore satisfies 7m/8 clauses in expectation, and conditional expectations can remove the randomness.
A constant gap is the key

Ordinary NP-hardness may separate full satisfaction from failure on one clause out of millions. Approximation hardness requires a robust gap. Håstad constructed PCPs giving essentially optimal gaps for MAX-E3SAT and MAX-E3LIN.
Decode a coordinate from a function

Long-code tests encode a label i as the dictator f(x)=xᵢ. Fourier analysis shows how unusually high acceptance reveals coordinates usable as labels. The test and predicate determine the quantitative hardness.
The constraint is uniquely satisfiable in one direction

Every edge carries a permutation π, requiring xᵥ=π(xᵤ). Once one endpoint label is chosen, the other is forced. Exact full satisfiability can be tested by propagation; the conjecture concerns robust approximation gaps.

The Unique Games Conjecture posits NP-hardness of distinguishing optimum at least 1−ε from optimum at most δ, for every fixed positive ε and δ with a sufficiently large fixed alphabet. Consequences below are conditional on this conjecture, not unconditional hardness theorems.

Khot, Kindler, Mossel and O’Donnell related MAX-CUT hardness to noise stability. Conditional on UGC, beating the Goemans–Williamson ratio by a fixed amount would be NP-hard. Raghavendra extended the relationship to a general fixed-CSP framework.
The characters χS(x)=∏ᵢ∈Sxᵢ form an orthonormal basis under the uniform measure on {−1,1}ⁿ. Every real-valued function on the cube has a unique expansion.
If each coordinate pair has correlation ρ, noise stability is ΣSρ^{|S|}f̂(S)². High-degree components are damped when |ρ|<1. For Boolean-valued f, coordinate influence is ΣS∋ᵢf̂(S)².

For fixed positive noise correlation, balanced Boolean functions with sufficiently small coordinate influences have stability at most the asymptotic majority value plus a small error. The Mossel–O’Donnell–Oleszkiewicz invariance principle transfers the problem toward Gaussian space.
A cut assigns each vertex a sign xᵢ. Its objective is Σwᵢⱼ(1−xᵢxⱼ)/2 for nonnegative edge weights. Replacing signs by unit vectors relaxes the discrete problem to an SDP.
Choose a rotationally symmetric Gaussian vector g and use the sign of ⟨g,vᵢ⟩. Two vectors at angle θ are separated with probability θ/π. Compare this with their SDP contribution (1−cosθ)/2.

The expected cut value is at least αGW times the SDP value and hence at least αGW times the true optimum, up to numerical precision. UGC-based hardness gives a matching threshold, but that optimality statement is conditional.

Fix a finite domain and a finite set of bounded-arity predicates. The task is to maximize the fraction or weight of satisfied constraints. This framework includes many, but not all, optimization problems.

The basic SDP combines vector correlations with local distributions on constraint scopes. Pairwise inner products alone do not describe arbitrary higher-arity constraints. A genuine assignment gives a feasible solution, while an SDP solution may not correspond to any global assignment.

Raghavendra connects the achievable rounding guarantees to matching Unique-Games-based hardness, with arbitrarily small slack. The theorem turns a problem-by-problem approximation search into a unified framework, though finding a simple closed-form threshold may still be difficult.

A distribution on Boolean assignments determines moments of every monomial. A relaxation retains moments only through degree 2d, expressed as a linear functional Ẽ. It must normalize 1 and annihilate the equality constraints at allowed degrees.
For monomials xᵅ of degree at most d, form Mᵅᵝ=Ẽ[xᵅ⁺ᵝ]. Requiring Ẽ[p²]≥0 for every degree-d polynomial p is equivalent to M being positive semidefinite.

As the level rises, feasible truncated moment sets become more restricted, and maximization upper bounds decrease. For Boolean problems, sufficiently high levels are exact. Fixed levels have SDP size n^{O(d)}, with numerical precision conditions still relevant.

The dual seeks bounded-degree sum-of-squares certificates modulo the constraints. General polynomial optimization needs appropriate compactness or positivity assumptions for convergence claims. A pseudoexpectation obstructs a low-degree certificate without necessarily describing a real probability measure.

The vertex update records a vertex’s old color and the multiset of its neighbors’ colors. Assign equal new colors exactly when these records agree. Run comparison with a common encoding, not unrelated color names in each graph.

Starting from one color, every vertex of a d-regular graph sees the same multiset forever. Two nonisomorphic d-regular graphs of equal order are therefore indistinguishable by this basic procedure. Rigidity and automorphism count are separate issues.

Higher-dimensional versions refine tuples. Precise correspondences with counting logic depend on conventions and indexing. Cai–Fürer–Immerman constructions give nonisomorphic graph families requiring linearly many variables to distinguish, exposing a global parity obstruction.

Directed reachability is NL-complete. Immerman and Szelepcsényi independently proved that its complement is in NL. The method tracks the number of vertices reachable within k steps rather than storing all of them.
Why a count makes the certificate trustworthy

Given the correct number of reachable vertices, a nondeterministic computation can enumerate witnessed reachable vertices and reject if the count is wrong. This supports an inductive update of the next reachable-set size using logarithmic workspace.

On finite structures equipped with a linear order, first-order logic with transitive closure captures NL, and least fixed-point logic captures P. The order hypothesis in the Immerman–Vardi theorem is essential to its stated form.

Every first-order sentence over a finite relational vocabulary is equivalent to a Boolean combination of basic local sentences. Such a sentence asks for finitely many sufficiently separated vertices, all satisfying a specified local formula.

For bounded-degree graph sequences, Benjamini–Schramm convergence records the probabilities of rooted neighborhoods. A rare feature can occur at one vertex and disappear from those probabilities, while an existential FO sentence still detects it.
Why algorithms need more than a radius

A fixed-radius ball can still be huge when degrees are unbounded. Algorithmic applications therefore combine locality with structural sparsity or other restrictions. Locality does not make arbitrary-graph model checking automatically easy.

Subdividing every edge of a clique once gives a graph of bounded average degree, but depth-one contractions recover the original clique. A useful sparsity notion must control what is revealed by local contraction.

Bounded expansion bounds the density of every fixed-depth shallow minor by a function of that depth. Nowhere density instead excludes sufficiently large clique shallow minors at each fixed depth. It is a weaker structural restriction.

Nešetřil and Ossona de Mendez developed the structural framework underlying important model-checking results. Dvořák–Král’–Thomas obtained linear-time FO model checking for bounded expansion, and Grohe–Kreutzer–Siebertz almost-linear algorithms for effectively nowhere-dense classes. Nešetřil’s work with Hell also made graph homomorphisms central to coloring and CSPs.

Open a profile, adjust its type size or line spacing, and use Focus to hide the surrounding navigation. The contents highlight your position as you scroll. A reading position is not a completion mark: only the Mark as read button changes your read list. Continue from Discover or the Recent shelf.

Every article section has its own shareable link. Equations open in a larger view with copyable plain text and, where it exists in the source, TeX. The pre-rendered mathematics needs no network connection.

Arrows retain their original labels and descriptions. Some denote collaborations; others are thematic reading connections. The route finder searches only those recorded edges. Exploring an arrow in reverse is explicitly identified and does not reverse its historical meaning.
The 12 idea lenses and question suggestions use text matching in this catalogue. They are navigation aids, not generated answers, scientific classifications or exhaustive literature surveys.

Notes, saved profiles and preferences remain in browser storage. There are no accounts, trackers, remote fonts, background requests or cloud uploads. All main actions have keyboard controls, visible focus indicators and text labels. The graph has an equivalent connection list, so dragging is never necessary for exploring its data. Dialogs support Escape and return focus to the opening control. Reduced-motion preferences are respected. A manual screen-reader audit has not been performed.
